scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A submarine can float on the surface, then sink deep underwater, then rise again. How does it control that?

scenes.name: tanks
scenes.text: Submarines have ballast tanks between the inner and outer hull, which can hold water or air.

scenes.name: dive
scenes.text: To dive, vents open and seawater floods the tanks. The submarine gets heavier than the water it displaces, and sinks.

scenes.name: surface
scenes.text: To surface, compressed air is blown into the tanks, pushing the water out. It becomes lighter and rises.

scenes.name: neutral
scenes.text: By balancing water and air carefully, it can stay at one depth, neither sinking nor rising.

scenes.name: planes
scenes.text: Small fins called diving planes tilt the submarine up or down as it moves, like wings underwater.

scenes.name: hull
scenes.text: Deep water pushes hard from all sides, so the inner pressure hull is built extremely strong.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Flood to dive, blow air to rise. Follow for more on how things really work.
